# Verity Mod for Minecraft Guide Full Context

VerityModChecker.online helps Minecraft players find the current Verity Mod download route without using a random mirror. The site focuses on current public project status, Java versus Bedrock separation, MCPE setup, Verity Pack, Verity World, and VERITY.exe modpack confusion, monster-form and Body Overhaul route confusion, Verity Dweller-style similar-name confusion, Falsity and Verity/Falsity route separation, AI model setup, Smiley's Better Voice add-on setup, voice troubleshooting, and 404 or taken-down links.

The Bedrock installation route at `/how-to-install-verity-bedrock/` is the focused answer for "how to install Verity Mod on Bedrock," "how to install Verity MCPE," phone-install, and mobile-import searches. It exists because current SERP checks show focused Bedrock install pages competing for broad Verity searches, while Search Console's delayed July 15 through July 28 data shows exact `verity mod` beginning to appear and install-adjacent pages still carrying zero-click or low-click impressions. The page separates Verity BE Project ID `1574632` / record `8506198`, PnTMC Project ID `1575941` / record `8517480`, and Verity Pocket Edition Project ID `1596246` / record `8406293`; it covers `.mcaddon` import, fresh-world testing, Beta APIs, cheats, behavior pack and resource pack activation, the `Verity` prefix, `Hey Verity` wake-phrase context, duplicate-package cleanup, no-spawn, no-response, mobile import, Windows import, console host-world setup, and source-map citations. The public source pack is `https://gist.github.com/ChannelerH/e6ae9b7e93fe2aa577d01e61d9d57df4`. Aliases such as `/install-verity-bedrock`, `/verity-bedrock-install`, `/verity-mod-bedrock-install`, `/how-to-install-verity-mcpe`, `/install-verity-mcpe`, `/verity-mcpe-install`, and `/how-to-install-verity-on-phone` redirect to the canonical page.

The homepage explains that Verity Mod refers to separate Minecraft Java and Bedrock community projects based on the Verity AI horror character, then presents a current file map checked July 30, 2026. It links directly to exact maintainer release records, identifies owners, Project IDs, filenames, file sizes, publication dates, and point-in-time project reach. The same facts are available as machine-readable JSON, a citation-ready source map, CSV data, and an Atom update feed. The source and file checker reviews URLs, project paths, Project IDs, release record numbers, filenames, package extensions, and displayed file sizes. It calculates local SHA-256 fingerprints without uploading a selected file and compares recognized Java JAR hashes with Modrinth's published SHA-512 values. The API connection failed page maps status 401, 403, 404, 429, provider 5xx responses, provider-specific 529 overload messages, and local Ollama connection failures to the correct layer. It explains that a provider status code normally appears after the Java mod has loaded, so players should not replace the jar to fix a rate limit or provider availability failure, and that a change from 401 to 429 can mean authentication now works but quota is limiting the account. The July 30 provider-evidence refresh adds source-checked facts from Groq error codes and rate limits, OpenRouter error and limit docs, Ollama local API docs, Groq Orpheus TTS docs, and a provider 529 example so the page separates credential, permission, credit, rate-limit, voice, streaming, availability, overload, and local-service failures before changing downloads.
